name: LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal Data
description: A multimodal dataset featuring audio, image, and textual data from 50 classes, specifically designed for learning from uncertain data. It extends the CIFAR 10/100 dataset with audio samples extracted from three audio corpora, and text data generated using the Gemma-7B Large Language Model. The dataset enables controlled injection of varying types and degrees of uncertainty for experiments and benchmarking initiatives.
citeAs: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, and Sébastien Fournier. 2025. LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal Data. In Proceedings of the 48th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR '25), July 13–18, 2025, Padua, Italy. ACM, New York, NY, USA, 10 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3726302.3730302
rai:dataCollection: The dataset includes 101,000 images from CIFAR-10/100, 135,096 speech audio recordings extracted from three audio corpora (The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, and Mozilla Common Voice), and 62,875 text passages generated using the Gemma-7B Instruct Large Language Model. Each modality is independently sourced, reflecting real-world conditions where data is often collected under different conditions and times.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Web API, Direct measurement
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images: CIFAR-10/100 dataset and EDM Diffusion-based generative model generated images. Audio: The Spoken Wikipedia corpus, LibriSpeech corpus (derived from LibriVox audiobooks), Mozilla Common Voice corpus, and 73 additional recordings voluntarily contributed by colleagues. Text: Generated using Gemma-7B Instruct Large Language Model based on class labels.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For audio modality: extracted audio segments corresponding to CIFAR-10/100 class labels using word-level alignments (phoneme-level for Spoken Wikipedia, forced alignments for LibriSpeech and Mozilla Common Voice using Montreal Forced Aligner). Audio samples were trimmed and anonymized. For text modality: masked all label occurrences in generated text and validated by feeding back into Gemma-7B Instruct model for classification. For images: sampled 600 data points with different levels of diversity from CIFAR-10/100 dataset.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio: Automatic validation using OpenAI's Whisper Large V3 model for transcription. Samples where transcription matched class label were considered valid. Samples that failed automatic validation were sent for manual validation. 130,069 out of 178,123 audio samples were validated automatically. Text: Generated texts were validated by masking label occurrences and using Gemma-7B Instruct for classification. 55,953 text samples were accepted. Bias detection was performed using Gemma model, and prompts were reconstructed for classes with high bias (man, woman, boy, girl) to reduce biases. Images: Deep features extracted using VGG-11 for diversity control. Audio features extracted using Wav2Vec, text features using BERT.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual validation was performed for 8,372 audio samples that did not pass automatic validation and belonged to classes with fewer than 800 samples. Annotators were asked 'Is the audio saying the word below? (An extra 's' or 'es' in the pronunciation is okay.)' with answer options of 'Yes' or 'No'. Two annotations were collected per sample from 17 annotators (M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors) with advanced to fluent English knowledge. 71.61% annotation agreement was achieved. 5,027 samples were accepted where both annotators confirmed validity. Samples with conflicting annotations were rejected.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For audio validation: 71.61% annotation agreement between annotators. Samples were accepted only when both annotators confirmed validity. Samples with conflicting annotations were rejected.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 annotations per audio sample for manual validation
rai:annotatorDemographics: 17 annotators including M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors with advanced to fluent English knowledge
rai:machineAnnotationTools: OpenAI's Whisper Large V3 model for audio transcription validation, Montreal Forced Aligner for word-level alignments in LibriSpeech and Mozilla Common Voice, Gemma-7B Instruct for text generation and validation
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes classes related to human attributes such as 'man', 'woman', 'boy', and 'girl'. Audio samples include pronunciations from diverse speakers with varying accents.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to promote and support the development, evaluation, and benchmarking of trustworthy and robust multimodal deep learning approaches for safety critical applications such as healthcare, autonomous driving, and finance.
rai:dataBiases: Gender bias was identified in text data, particularly for classes 'man', 'woman', 'boy', and 'girl'. The Gemma model identified high levels of gender bias in these classes. Prompts were reconstructed to explicitly provide topics and keywords with occupations to minimize bias. After reconstruction, significant bias still exists but enough unbiased texts were identified for inclusion. The authors note that describing a man or woman in an unbiased way is challenging for LLM models trained on unbalanced data. The dataset may contain factual inaccuracies or biases due to LLM generation.
rai:dataLimitations: Since textual data was generated using an LLM, the dataset may contain factual inaccuracies or biases. LUMA shall not be used as a source of knowledge or information. The dataset is specifically designed for benchmarking multimodal learning algorithms on uncertain data and studying uncertainty quantification in multimodal classification settings. Audio samples from forced alignments may include misaligned segments introducing additional noise. Some audio samples may be very noisy or have strong accents that are hard to interpret.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for: 1) Training, testing, and validation of multimodal deep learning models; 2) Benchmarking multimodal learning algorithms on uncertain data; 3) Studying uncertainty quantification in multimodal classification settings; 4) Developing trustworthy and robust machine learning approaches for safety critical applications; 5) Research on aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty in multimodal contexts; 6) Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection research. The dataset consists of 600 data records per class (500 for training, 100 for testing) belonging to 42 classes, and 3,859 OOD data points belonging to 8 remaining classes.
